title: Rewrite a world-knowledge leak by hand
statement: When general knowledge answers an item, rewrite it by hand rather than tie it to obscure passage details, which raises difficulty without testing the targeted skill.
detail: An analysis of a regenerate-on-leak plan for a Grade 5 reading bank found regeneration the wrong tool for a large share of leaks: items answerable from world knowledge or general reasoning can't be honestly locked to the passage, and forcing it turns a science-reasoning item into an obscurity item, harder without testing more of the targeted skill. Its plan regenerates passage-locked replacements only for leaks caused by construction flaws, such as weak distractors or tells in the options, and flags world-knowledge leaks for a person to rewrite.
against: It is a plan: at the time nothing consumed the regeneration requests, so the split between kinds of leak was never tried (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course-candidate-v0/GOAL_ANALYSIS.md`, lines 92 and 168).

evidence.quote: (3) Regeneration is the **wrong tool for a large share of leaks** — world-knowledge/general-reasoning leaks (~27 sequence-id/world-knowledge) can't be honestly passage-locked; doing so converts a science-reasoning item into an *obscurity* item (raises difficulty without raising the targeted skill — the transfer trap).
flag world-knowledge leaks for human rewrite, not auto-passage-lock.
